name: Lean Mediterranean
summary: Big salads, brothy soups and roasted vegetables from Greece, Italy and Spain, built around lean protein, beans and plenty of fibre. It is generous Mediterranean food, built to keep you full on fewer calories.
howItWorks:
**Protein at every meal.** Chicken, cod, turkey, shrimp, pork tenderloin, tuna, nonfat Greek yogurt and egg whites all carry real protein, and sardines on Friday and salmon on Sunday add omega-3 and vitamin D. Protein is the most filling thing on the plate, so a smaller meal still feels like a proper one.

**Volume and fibre first.** Big salads, fennel, cabbage, a brothy soup and a tray of roasted vegetables fill the plate, and white beans, chickpeas, lentils or lupini turn up every day. Together they bring **plenty of fibre** and take up room, so you feel full before the food runs out.

**Cook once, eat twice.** The Greek chicken salad, cod stew, keftedes, lentejas and souvlaki each make two portions, so the next day's lunch is already done, and the frittata covers Sunday's breakfast. On Friday night, marinate the pork for Saturday's souvlaki.

**Flavour without fuss.** Lemon, vinegar, oregano, capers, olives, smoked paprika and a little feta do the work, so nothing tastes like diet food.

**What Light changes.** Every meal keeps its vegetables, and the cod, turkey, shrimp, pork, tuna, sardines and salmon stay much the same. Light trims the pita, oil, feta, olives and walnuts, some of the beans, chicken, egg whites and breakfast yogurt, and keeps one snack a day. Each plate still looks like a meal.

recipes.name: Greek yogurt with pear, walnuts and cinnamon
recipes.inspiredBy: Greek yiaourti me karydia, the everyday bowl of thick yogurt and nuts
recipes.about: Thick nonfat Greek yogurt with sliced pear, a handful of toasted walnuts and a dusting of cinnamon. It feels like a treat but carries **a big helping of protein**, so it keeps you going well past mid-morning.
steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, shaking now and then, until they smell nutty. Tip them onto a plate to cool, then chop roughly.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and fan the pear slices over it.
Scatter on the warm walnuts and dust with cinnamon.
recipes.tip: Toast a jar of walnuts on Sunday and breakfast takes two minutes. Swap the pear for whatever fruit is in season: apple, plums or a few grapes all work.

recipes.name: Kagianas-style tomato eggs with feta and warm pita
recipes.inspiredBy: Greek kagianas, eggs scrambled into juicy tomatoes, with extra egg whites for protein
recipes.about: Ripe tomatoes cooked down until jammy, then softly scrambled with one whole egg, a few extra whites and a little crumbled feta. It is a very Greek breakfast, and the whites give it **a big protein hit** for few calories.

ingredients.note: from a carton or separated eggs
warmed, cut into strips for scooping

steps: Warm the olive oil in a small pan over medium heat and soften the onion for about 3 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, a pinch of salt and the oregano. Cook for 6 to 8 minutes, mashing with the spoon, until the juices have mostly cooked away and the tomatoes look jammy.
Whisk the egg and egg whites together and pour them into the tomatoes. Stir gently over low heat for 2 to 3 minutes until softly set and still glossy.
Crumble in the feta, scatter with parsley, add a squeeze of lemon and serve with the warm pita.
recipes.tip: Keep a carton of liquid egg whites in the fridge, so you are not left with a bowl of yolks. One white is about 2 tablespoons.

recipes.name: Spinach, zucchini and feta frittata
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Italian frittata and Greek spanakopita filling
recipes.about: A thick, herby oven frittata packed with spinach and zucchini, mostly egg whites with two whole eggs for flavour and colour. It makes two portions, so the second one is **a cold breakfast ready** for tomorrow.

ingredients.note: 1 large egg per serving, so 2 in the pan
about 3 whites per serving, so 6 or 7 in the pan

steps: Heat the oven to 180 C. Warm the olive oil in an oven-safe 20 cm pan over medium heat and soften the onion for 3 minutes.
Add the grated zucchini and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until it has given up its water and is soft. Add the spinach by the handful until it wilts, about 2 minutes.
Whisk the eggs and the egg whites with the salt, pepper, dill, parsley and lemon juice. Pour over the vegetables and dot with the feta.
Cook on the stove for 1 minute to set the edges, then bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until just set and still slightly soft in the middle. Do not overbake, or the whites turn rubbery.
Cut it in half. Serve one half warm with the sliced tomato, cucumber and pita. Cool the other half, cover and refrigerate for tomorrow.
recipes.tip: Reheat it gently, or eat it cold from the fridge with the tomato and cucumber, which is just as good.

recipes.name: Tuna, white bean and spinach salad
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Tuscan tonno e fagioli
recipes.about: The Tuscan classic: tender white beans, good tuna, red onion and lemon, piled on baby spinach with capers for salt and bite. **Beans and tuna together** give you protein and fibre that fill you up on one plate.
steps: Soak the red onion slices in the lemon juice and vinegar for 5 minutes while you prep. It softens the bite.
Toss the beans with the shaved fennel, parsley, capers, olive oil and the onion with its juices. Season with pepper.
Pile the spinach on a big plate, spoon the beans over it and flake the tuna on top.
Serve with the warm pita.
recipes.tip: Use a tin of tuna packed in water, drained well, and let the olive oil in the dressing do the richness.

recipes.name: Big Greek salad with lemon-oregano chicken
recipes.inspiredBy: Greek horiatiki, with grilled chicken, chickpeas and a bed of baby spinach to make it a meal
recipes.about: Juicy lemon-oregano chicken over a big bowl of baby spinach, cucumber, tomato, peppers and olives, with feta and chickpeas. The plate is huge but light, and the **chicken, chickpeas and feta** carry the protein. It makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done.

ingredients.note: half for the chicken, half for the dressing

steps: Slice the chicken breasts in half horizontally so they are thin. Rub with half the lemon juice, the garlic, half the oregano and a pinch of salt. Leave for 10 minutes or up to a few hours.
Heat a grill pan or heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for 3 to 4 minutes a side, until golden and no pink remains. Rest for 5 minutes, then slice.
Whisk the olive oil, the red wine vinegar, the rest of the lemon juice and the rest of the oregano in a jar. Chop the cucumber, tomato, onion and pepper.

Toss half the chopped vegetables, half the chickpeas and half the olives with half the dressing in a big bowl. Fold in half the spinach, top with half the chicken and half the feta, and serve with the warm pita.

Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch: the vegetables, chickpeas, olives, spinach, chicken and feta in one container, and the rest of the dressing in a small jar. Toss it together when you eat so everything stays crisp.
recipes.tip: No grill pan? Roast the thin cutlets at 220 C for 10 to 12 minutes instead.

recipes.name: Cod, white bean and fennel stew with saffron
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Spanish cod and white bean stews, with fennel and saffron
recipes.about: Flaky cod simmered in a saffron and fennel tomato broth with creamy white beans and a handful of spinach. It is light and deeply savoury, and the **cod, beans and greens** make a very filling bowl for the calories. Two portions: dinner now, lunch tomorrow.

ingredients.note: passata or crushed tomatoes, no salt added (not paste)
warmed, cut into strips for dunking in the broth

steps: Warm the olive oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Cook the fennel and onion for 8 minutes, until soft and just turning golden at the edges. Add the garlic for the last minute.
Crumble in the saffron, then add the passata, the beans, 150 ml of water, the salt and pepper. Simmer for 10 minutes until it tastes like a proper stew.
Stir in the spinach until it wilts. Nestle in the cod, cover, and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, until it flakes easily.
Finish with the lemon juice and parsley. Serve in wide bowls with the warm pita for the broth.
Cool the second portion and keep it in the fridge. Reheat gently tomorrow, so the fish stays tender.
recipes.tip: Hake, haddock or any white fish works, and so does a handful of frozen peas at the end.

recipes.name: Turkey keftedes in tomato sauce with zucchini and bulgur
recipes.inspiredBy: Greek keftedes, made with lean turkey and oats, in a simple tomato sauce
recipes.about: Herby baked meatballs scented with mint and oregano, simmered in tomato sauce with zucchini and chard, over fluffy bulgur. Fat-free ground turkey keeps them **high in protein**, and grated onion, zucchini and a few oats keep them tender. They reheat beautifully.

ingredients.note: 1 or 2 egg whites for the whole batch, as binder
grated and squeezed, for the meat mix
passata or crushed tomatoes, no salt added (not paste)

steps: Heat the oven to 200 C and line a tray. Mix the turkey, egg white, oats, grated onion, grated zucchini, the grated garlic, parsley, mint, oregano, most of the salt and the pepper with your hands until it just holds together. Roll into about 16 small balls.
Bake the keftedes for 14 minutes, turning once, until browned and cooked through.

Meanwhile, warm the olive oil in a wide pan and soften the sliced garlic for 30 seconds. Add the passata, diced zucchini, the last pinch of salt and a splash of water. Simmer for 10 minutes, until the zucchini is tender.
Stir in the chard, then slide the keftedes into the sauce and simmer for 5 minutes.
Cook the bulgur in twice its volume of boiling water for about 12 minutes, until tender. Fluff with a fork. At the Light size this is just a few spoonfuls, enough to catch the sauce.
Serve the keftedes and sauce over the bulgur with a squeeze of lemon. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
recipes.tip: Roll a double batch of keftedes and freeze half raw on a tray, then bag them.

recipes.name: Spanish lentils with garlic shrimp and chard
recipes.inspiredBy: Spanish lentejas, with garlic shrimp (gambas) instead of chorizo
recipes.about: A pot of tender green lentils in a smoky pimentón sofrito, finished with sherry vinegar and garlicky shrimp. The **lentils and shrimp together** are a lot of protein for a modest plate, with iron from the lentils and chard, and the sherry vinegar brightens everything. It makes two portions.

ingredients.note: passata or crushed tomatoes, no salt added (not paste)
peeled and deveined, plain (the bag should list only shrimp)

steps: Warm half the olive oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrot and pepper for 8 minutes, until soft and sweet. Add half the garlic and the pimentón and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the lentils, passata, bay leaf, salt and enough water to cover by 3 cm. Simmer for 25 to 30 minutes, until the lentils are tender but still hold their shape.
Stir in the chard for the last 5 minutes until tender, then take off the heat and stir in the sherry vinegar.
Heat the rest of the oil in a skillet over high heat. Sear the shrimp with the rest of the garlic in two batches so they brown rather than steam, about 90 seconds each, until pink and curled.

Ladle half the lentils into a bowl, top with half the shrimp and the parsley. Keep the rest of the lentils and shrimp apart in the fridge for tomorrow, and warm the shrimp just through so they stay tender.
recipes.tip: Freeze the lentils alone for up to 3 months and cook fresh shrimp whenever you reheat.

recipes.name: Sicilian-style sardine, fennel and orange salad with chickpeas
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Sicilian sardine and fennel pairings, with orange and olives
recipes.about: Crisp shaved fennel, juicy orange and peppery arugula with canned sardines, chickpeas and a few olives. The sweet and sharp mix is a classic, and the **sardines bring omega-3 and calcium** from their soft bones.

ingredients.note: canned in olive oil, drained, bones in

steps: Shave the fennel as thinly as you can with a knife or mandoline, and keep the feathery fronds.
Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice and vinegar in a big bowl. Add the fennel, chickpeas, onion and olives and toss.
Lay the arugula on a plate, spoon the fennel mix over it and add the orange rounds.
Top with the sardines, broken into big pieces, then the parsley, fennel fronds and a sprinkle of Aleppo pepper. Serve with the warm pita.
recipes.tip: Salad too sharp? Add a few more orange slices. Fresh sardines, grilled, are lovely here when you can get them.

recipes.name: Pork souvlaki with tzatziki, cabbage salad and pita
recipes.inspiredBy: Greek souvlaki, with a winter lahano salad instead of fries
recipes.about: Lemon, oregano and garlic pork skewers with a thick garlicky tzatziki, a crunchy lemony cabbage and carrot salad and a warm pita. The pork tenderloin is very lean and the **nonfat yogurt sauce** adds protein, not just flavour. It is the weekend project of the week, and it makes two portions.
steps: Cut the pork into 3 cm cubes. Mix with half the lemon juice, half the oil, half the garlic, the oregano, half the salt and the pepper. Leave for at least 1 hour in the fridge, or overnight.
For the tzatziki, stir together the yogurt, grated cucumber, the rest of the garlic, half the dill and a squeeze of lemon. Chill until needed.
Toss the cabbage and carrot with the rest of the lemon juice and oil, the parsley, the remaining dill and a pinch of salt. Leave it for 10 minutes so the cabbage softens a little.
Thread the pork onto skewers, soaked first if they are wooden. Grill or broil for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until browned and just cooked through. Warm the pita on the grill for the last minute.
Serve half the pork and tzatziki with the cabbage salad and pita. Chill the rest, kept apart, for tomorrow.
recipes.tip: Tomorrow, slice the cold pork over the salad and spoon the tzatziki on top.

recipes.name: Chicken, chickpea and chard soup with lemon
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Greek lemony chicken soups and Spanish chicken and chickpea pots
recipes.about: A bright, brothy soup with shredded chicken, chickpeas, carrots and plenty of chard, finished with lots of lemon and dill. It is warming but light, and the **chicken and chickpeas** give you plenty of protein.
steps: Warm the olive oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion and carrot for 6 minutes, until soft and golden. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the chicken whole, the chickpeas, the oregano, bay leaf, salt, pepper and 450 ml of water. Bring to a simmer and cook gently for 12 to 15 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
Lift out the chicken and shred it with two forks. Return it to the pot with the chard and cook for 4 minutes, until the chard is tender.
Take off the heat, stir in the lemon juice and dill, and serve with the warm pita.
recipes.tip: Saturday is a cooking day, so make the soup on Friday evening while you put the sardine salad together, and add the lemon and dill when you reheat it. For an avgolemono finish, whisk one egg with the lemon juice, stir in a ladle of hot broth, then stir it back in off the heat.

recipes.name: Roasted salmon with tomatoes, artichokes and white beans
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Cretan baked fish and vegetables
recipes.about: A tray of zucchini, peppers, tomatoes, artichoke hearts and olives roasted until sweet and jammy, with a salmon fillet laid on top and white beans warmed in the juices. The **salmon brings omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the tray is mostly vegetables.

ingredients.note: wild sockeye, fresh or thawed from frozen, skin on or off
frozen artichoke hearts, thawed and halved

steps: Heat the oven to 220 C. Toss the zucchini, pepper, tomatoes and onion with half the olive oil, the oregano, salt and pepper on a big tray. Roast for 20 minutes, until soft and starting to blister.
Stir in the beans, artichoke hearts, olives and capers and make a gap in the middle of the tray.
Rub the salmon with the rest of the oil and lay it in the gap. Roast for 6 to 8 minutes, until it just flakes. Wild salmon is lean, so take it out the moment it does.
Squeeze over the lemon juice, scatter with parsley and add a pinch of Aleppo pepper if you like.
recipes.tip: Chop the vegetables a little smaller and they roast faster. Any leftover roasted vegetables are lovely cold in a pita. Coho or farmed salmon work too.

recipes.name: Lupini beans with lemon, olives and parsley
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Spanish altramuces and Italian lupini
recipes.about: Firm, nutty lupini beans from the jar, dressed with lemon, parsley and a few olives. Lupini are **unusually high in protein**, so this little bowl is a satisfying, salty snack.
steps: Rinse the lupini well and drain them, then pat dry.
Toss with the lemon juice, parsley, olives, olive oil and Aleppo pepper.
recipes.tip: Pinch the skins off if you like: they slip right off, but they are fine to eat.

recipes.name: Orange and walnuts
recipes.about: Juicy orange segments with a small handful of walnuts, a sweet and crunchy snack. The orange covers **a full day of vitamin C** and the walnuts add omega-3 fat.
steps: Peel the orange and break it into segments.
Serve with the walnuts in a small bowl.

recipes.name: Dried figs with walnuts
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Greek sika me karydia, figs with walnuts
recipes.about: Chewy dried figs with a small handful of walnuts, the classic Greek pairing. The figs bring **fibre and a little calcium** and the walnuts add omega-3 fat.
steps: Halve the figs.
Serve with the walnuts.

recipes.name: Roasted chickpeas with smoked paprika
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Spanish garbanzos fritos, roasted not fried
recipes.about: Crunchy oven-roasted chickpeas with smoked paprika and a little cumin. They are an easy, **fibre-rich** way to scratch the crunchy itch.
steps: Heat the oven to 220 C. Drain the chickpeas and pat them very dry with a clean towel.
Toss with the olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin and salt on a tray.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, shaking the tray halfway, until crisp and deep golden.
recipes.tip: They are crispiest the day you make them. Roast a double batch on Wednesday alongside the keftedes (give them 30 to 35 minutes at 200 C) and keep the rest in a jar for Friday.

recipes.name: Cannellini and garlic dip with crunchy vegetables
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Tuscan crema di cannellini
recipes.about: A smooth, lemony cannellini dip with garlic and olive oil, scooped up with cucumber and carrot. It is **creamy and filling** without any cream.
steps: Mash or blitz the beans with the lemon juice, garlic, olive oil and a splash of water until smooth.
Spoon into a bowl, drizzle with a few drops of the oil, dust with oregano and serve with the carrot and cucumber sticks.
recipes.tip: Make a double batch on Tuesday and keep half covered in the fridge for Wednesday's snack.

recipes.name: Tzatziki with pepper and carrot sticks
recipes.about: A big scoop of thick nonfat Greek yogurt tzatziki with cucumber, garlic and dill, for dipping crunchy pepper and carrot. It is **a protein-rich snack** that tastes like a meze.
steps: Stir the yogurt with the grated cucumber, garlic, dill, lemon juice, olive oil and salt.
Serve with the carrot and pepper sticks for dipping.
